recognize_zh: 紅血球像疊起來的硬幣排成長鏈，中央一條長串超過十顆、邊緣彼此重疊，背景呈淡粉紅色（血漿蛋白增加）；這種線狀疊錢排列就是 rouleaux formation。
features: Red cells stacked in linear coin-like chains of up to more than 10 cells
Stacks show overlapping curved borders with preserved individual outlines
Short stacks and branching chains throughout the field
Pinkish-tan background suggesting increased plasma protein
Scattered spherocytic-appearing and crenated red cells, few platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows extensive rouleaux formation, with red cells aligned in linear and branching stacks resembling piles of coins, some exceeding ten cells in length. The background has a faint pinkish-blue protein tint. Occasional crenated and rounded red cells without central pallor are also present, and irregular grape-like clumps typical of agglutination are not seen. Findings are consistent with rouleaux formation, suggesting elevated plasma proteins such as a monoclonal immunoglobulin or fibrinogen; serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation is recommended.

ddx.vs: Agglutination produces irregular three-dimensional clumps rather than orderly linear stacks, and often corrects with warming.
Artifactual stacking is confined to the thick part of the smear, whereas true rouleaux persists in the thin monolayer area.
Morphology is identical; separation requires protein electrophoresis and immunofixation to exclude a monoclonal protein.
